title: Kenyan Millet Porridge
author: Mama Wanjiru

relatedDish.note: KEN109 (Millet Porridge in Breads & Breakfast) and KEN029 (Traditional Kenyan Uji wa Wimbi in the original collection) describe the same dish. KEN029 includes the full heritage and cultural notes. KEN109 serves users browsing the Breads & Breakfast category.

desc: Uji wa Wimbi — Kenya's most universally consumed breakfast. Warm finger millet porridge, gently sweetened with sugar or honey and finished with milk. Nourishing, gluten-free, and beloved across every Kenyan community from infancy to old age.
longDesc: Every Kenyan who has had a hard morning knows the comfort of a cup of uji wa wimbi. The slightly earthy, nutty finger millet flour transforms into a smooth, warm, dark porridge with gentle sweetening and a splash of milk. It is the first food of infants, the breakfast of farmers, and the comfort of the elderly — a food that connects generations.
steps: Mix millet flour with 1 cup cold water until completely smooth — no lumps.
Bring remaining 3 cups water to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium. Pour millet slurry in a steady stream while stirring constantly.
Continue stirring for 5—7 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Add sugar or honey. Stir to dissolve.
Add milk if using. Simmer 2 more minutes.
Serve hot in cups or bowls.
chefTips: Always make a cold water slurry first — adding dry flour to boiling water creates lumps.
Stir constantly after adding the slurry — the moment you stop, lumps form.
Adjust thickness by adding more water for a thinner, drinkable porridge.
commonMistakes: Dry flour into boiling water — always make a slurry first.
cookingScience: Making a cold slurry distributes starch granules evenly in water before gelatinisation begins. This prevents clumping by ensuring each granule is surrounded by water before heat causes rapid swelling. See KEN029 for the full science explanation.
sustainabilityTips: Finger millet is one of the most drought-resistant cereals in Africa.
One of the most nutritious cereals per acre of land.
reheating: Add water and warm gently over low heat, stirring.
healthBenefits: Extraordinary calcium content — one of the best plant sources.
Rich in iron and essential amino acids.
culturalNote: Uji wa Wimbi is Kenya's most universally consumed breakfast — from hospital wards to homesteads, from school canteens to corporate cafeterias. See KEN029 for the full cultural story.
